discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases of matter
motivation: Kane and Mele showed (2005) that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological insulator, characterized by a Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states, the quantum spin Hall effect. Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe quantum wells (2007), measuring quantized edge conductance, and established the phenomenon experimentally. This work opened the field of symmetry-protected topological matter, soon extended to three-dimensional topological insulators, topological crystalline phases and Weyl semimetals. For superconductivity its impact is equally deep: the Fu-Kane proposal of proximity-induced Majorana states at topological insulator/superconductor interfaces launched the search for topological superconductivity and non-Abelian quasiparticles, and unified Andreev bound states, edge states and odd-frequency pairing under one topological framework. The discovery combines conceptual clarity, sharp testable predictions and decisive transport experiments, and it has reshaped condensed matter physics worldwide.
